title: Company Information — Guide
subtitle: A read-only training walkthrough with sample data and an explanation of every section

entry.tooltip: Open the visual guide for this page with sample data

demoBanner: Training mode — all data on this page is sample data shown for demonstration only. Nothing is saved or changed here and every control is read-only.

labels.realControlNote: The real control for this section is shown below, in read-only mode.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.intro: To fill in a company's information, follow these steps in order:
steps: From the card at the top, choose a company in “Select a company to edit…” (you can type a name, national ID, or code in the search box). Until you select one, nothing is shown.
After selecting, a blue “Edit mode:” badge with the company name appears and all sections load. If the title turns red with a “You have view-only access” banner, you may not edit.
Complete the “Name History” section with the “Add” button: start date and at least one name (first translation) are required; leaving the end date empty means it is the current name.
Fill in “Registration & Legal”: registration date, number, national ID, economic code, then choose country → province → city. Note this section does NOT auto-save.
Enter contact data: emails (address required), phones (E.164 format, + and 7–15 digits) and addresses (country/province/city, street 1 and postal code). These three sections auto-save.
In “Stakeholders”, add related people/companies with stakeholder type, ownership %, share count and dates as needed.
Finally, to save “Registration & Legal”, press the “Update Company” button in the “Operations” card and wait for the “Company updated successfully” message.

items.title: Auto-save vs. manual save
items.body: All grids (name history, emails, phones, addresses, stakeholders) save immediately on every add/edit/delete. The only exception is “Registration & Legal”, which saves only via the “Update Company” button.

items.title: Selecting a company gates everything
items.body: Until a company is selected, no section renders. The selection is remembered in the browser and stays selected on your next visit.

items.title: View-only access
items.body: If your access level on the company is 1, the page title turns red with a “You have view-only access” banner; all fields are disabled and the add/edit/delete buttons and the Operations card are removed.

items.title: Feedback messages
items.body: After each action a toast appears at the top: “Created successfully”, “Updated successfully”, “Deleted successfully”; on error, a red toast with a translated message.

selection.title: Select company
selection.intro: This card sits at the top and is the starting point. You use it to choose an existing company to edit; until one is selected, no other section is shown. (Creating a new company is done on the separate “Create company” page.)
steps: Click the “Select a company to edit…” box to open the company list.
Type a name, national ID, or code in the search box to filter the list.
Click the company you want; a check appears next to it and the “Edit mode:” badge shows its name.
To clear the selection, click the × button next to the box; all sections hide again.
tips: The selection is saved automatically and kept between visits; no button is needed for the selection itself.
If you lose access to the saved company or it is deleted, the selection is cleared automatically and the form resets.
The company name is not changed from this badge; do it from the “Name History” section.

nameHistory.title: Name history
nameHistory.intro: The company's name history over time. Each row is a name period (start date, end date and a reason note), and for each period the name can be stored in multiple languages (Persian and Latin). A row with no end date is the company's current name.
steps: Click “Add” to open the “Add new name change” dialog.
Pick a “Start date” (required), optionally fill the “End date” (empty = current name) and write a “Description”.
In “Company name (first translation)” pick a “Language” and enter the “Company name” (both required), then click “Add”.
To manage the name in other languages, click the “Translations” icon; add, edit or delete a translation.
To delete a whole name period, click the trash icon in the actions column.
tips: Only one translation per language is allowed; if every language is used, “Add translation” is disabled.
The Persian translation is the base name and cannot be deleted, only edited.
The displayed name for each row follows the current UI language; if that language is missing, the base name is shown.

registrationLegal.title: Registration & legal
registrationLegal.intro: The company's registration data: registration date and number, place of registration (country/province/city), national ID and economic code. This is the only section that does NOT auto-save — you must press “Update Company” after editing it.
steps: Pick the registration date from the calendar and enter the registration number.
Enter the national ID and economic code.
Choose the place of registration in cascading order: country, then province, then city.
To save, go to the “Operations” card at the bottom and press “Update Company”.
tips: The red stars are visual hints; final validation happens on the server and returns an error toast if something is missing.
If the province or city list looks empty, select the higher level first (country then province).
If you edit this section but do not press “Update Company”, the changes are not saved.

emails.title: Emails
emails.intro: The company's list of emails. For each email you can set a label, the address and a “Primary” flag. The “Verified” status is display-only and set by the system.
steps: Click “Add”; pick a label, enter the email address (required), optionally tick “Primary”, then “Add”.
To edit, click the pencil icon; to delete, click the trash icon in the same row.
All changes auto-save; no “Update Company” button is needed.
tips: The “Primary” label is not the same as the “Primary” tick; the label is just a name, while the tick decides which email is the company's primary one.
You cannot change the “Verified” status yourself.

phones.title: Phones
phones.intro: The company's phone numbers with label, number and a “Primary” flag. The number must be in international E.164 format.
steps: Click “Add” and pick a phone label (default: Landline).
Enter the number in E.164 format: a + sign then 7–15 digits (e.g. +982112345678).
Optionally tick “Primary” and click “Add” (the button stays disabled until the number is valid).
tips: The number must start with + and the country code; a local number without + is not valid.
While typing, invalid characters are stripped automatically; only digits and + remain.

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.intro: The company's addresses with label, location (country/province/city), street, postal code and a “Primary” flag. Location selection is cascading.
steps: Click “Add” and pick the address “Label” (default: Head office).
Choose the country; then the province and the city become enabled.
Enter “Address (street 1)” and the postal code; put extra details in “Street 2” if needed.
Optionally tick “Primary” and click “Add”/“Save”.
tips: If you don't see the province or city, select the higher level first.
Changing the country after filling the form clears the province, city and postal code.
The allowed postal-code length is validated based on the selected country.

stakeholders.title: Stakeholders
stakeholders.intro: People or companies that have an ownership/shareholding relationship with this company (e.g. parent company, shareholder, investor). For each stakeholder, the relationship type, ownership %, share count, dates and the board representative are recorded.
steps: Click “Add” to open the “Add stakeholder” dialog.
Pick the “Stakeholder type” (default: Shareholder).
Choose the related-party type (Person or Company), then search and select the related party.
Enter ownership %, share count, registration date and effective date (all four required), then click “Add”.
To view history, click the arrow at the start of the row (enabled only when history exists).
tips: Registration date vs. effective date: the registration date is when the record was created; the effective date is when the ownership state becomes valid.
The main table columns always show the latest (current) state; use the history arrow for previous values.
In this training sample, the related-party name shows as “unknown” because it is not connected to real person/company data.

operations.title: Operations & saving
operations.intro: The final card on the page. It holds the reminder “All operations are saved automatically, except Registration & Legal” and the “Update Company” button.
tips: The “Update Company” button saves only the “Registration & Legal” section; the other sections are already auto-saved.
This button is disabled only while “Processing…” or when no company is selected.
In view-only mode this card and button are removed entirely.

items.q: Why can't I see any part of the form?
items.a: Because you haven't selected a company yet. Until you pick one from the card at the top, none of the sections are shown. Select a company first.

items.q: I edited “Registration & Legal” but it didn't save, why?
items.a: This is the only section that does not auto-save. After filling it in, press the “Update Company” button in the “Operations” card to save it.

items.q: The title turned red with a “view-only” message; what does that mean?
items.a: It means your access level on this company is view-only. All fields are disabled and the add/edit/delete buttons and the Operations card are removed.

items.q: The company I had selected disappeared and the form went blank, why?
items.a: If you no longer have access to that company or it was deleted, the system clears the selection automatically so the form resets.

items.q: Why can't I change the “Verified” status of an email/phone/address?
items.a: The “Verified” column is display-only and set by the system; you can only set the “Primary” flag.

items.q: Where do I change the company name?
items.a: Name changes are made from the “Name History” section; each name period has a start/end date, and a name with no end date is the company's current name.
